AI.motivation: To investigate whether EWL quantization can induce evolutionary stability in games where the classical interior mixed Nash equilibrium is not evolutionarily stable, and to test whether such stabilization is robust under full quantum strategy space.
AI.method: The paper analyzes evolutionary stability under EWL quantization in a symmetric 2x2 game, comparing the restricted two-parameter EWL strategy space with the full three-parameter SU(2) strategy space.
AI.result: In the restricted two-parameter space, the quantum equilibrium s*=(π/2,π/4) becomes a strict symmetric Nash equilibrium and ESS for any γ>0. In the full SU(2) space, it remains a Nash equilibrium but strictness and the second ESS condition fail due to payoff-neutral mutants.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement stabilizes the equilibrium only within the restricted EWL strategy space; the stabilization effect does not survive enlargement to full SU(2), so the result is not robust.

title: Approximate Quantum State Preparation Through Proximal Policy Optimization
summary: In this work, a quantum architecture search framework for approximate quantum state preparation (QSP) is proposed. QSP is a challenging task, since the search space grows exponentially with the number of qubits, making the identification of the optimal circuit non-trivial. To address this problem, deep reinforcement learning is employed through an agent based on proximal policy optimization. The objective of the agent is to identify the best possible approximation of the target state while simultaneously minimizing the number of gates used. At each step, the agent appends a new gate to the circuit and recomputes the fidelity between the approximated state and the target states. Various experiments have been performed from 2 to 5 qubits. Both predefined states, such as Bell, GHZ, W, and Dicke states, and completely random states are considered. The proposed framework is able to achieve approximation errors of $10^{-14}$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a quantum architecture search framework using deep reinforcement learning (PPO) for approximate quantum state preparation, achieving approximation errors as low as 10^{-14} on 2-5 qubit systems for both predefined and random states.
AI.motivation: QSP is challenging because the search space grows exponentially with qubit count, making optimal circuit identification difficult. Existing approaches struggle with this scalability issue.
AI.method: Uses deep reinforcement learning with a PPO-based agent that iteratively appends gates to the circuit and recomputes fidelity. The agent balances approximation quality and gate count minimization.
AI.result: Achieves approximation errors of 10^{-14} on 2-5 qubit systems for Bell, GHZ, W, Dicke, and random states.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively addresses QSP scalability challenges using RL, producing high-fidelity approximations with minimal gate counts.

title: Duality constrains optimal thresholds in quantum error correction
summary: Error correction thresholds are often treated as the primary figure of merit for comparing quantum error-correcting code families. We show that the optimal error correction threshold for many commonly considered codes is constrained to a single universal value at leading order in a replica limit. Through a statistical mechanical mapping, we demonstrate that duality constrains all zero-rate em-symmetric CSS codes to have the same optimal code capacity threshold. Here, em symmetry means that the X- and Z-type parity-check matrices are equivalent up to row and column permutations. Under this statistical mechanical mapping, em-symmetric CSS codes are self-dual under a generalized Kramers-Wannier duality up to a mixing of logical sectors. For zero-rate code families, this mixing contributes only subextensive corrections, so the thermodynamic bulk free energy is self-dual in the trivial logical sector. This self-duality fixes the clean critical point and constrains the disordered phase boundary. We also show that self-duality is preserved under code concatenation, and that optimal decoding of concatenated codes can be reformulated as a renormalization group flow on a hierarchical lattice. Our results provide a common framework for analyzing topological, concatenated, and more general quantum low-density parity-check code families, including both their optimal code capacity thresholds and their sub-threshold logical error suppression.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that optimal error correction thresholds for many zero-rate, em-symmetric CSS codes converge to a single universal value at leading order, explained via statistical mechanical mapping and self-duality under a generalized Kramers-Wannier duality. This framework unifies topological, concatenated, and general quantum LDPC codes.
AI.motivation: To understand why many seemingly different quantum error-correcting code families exhibit similar optimal thresholds, and to provide a unifying theoretical framework beyond code-specific analyses.
AI.method: Statistical mechanical mapping of quantum error correction to a disorder model; replica limit analysis; demonstration of em-symmetry (equivalence of X and Z parity-check matrices up to permutations) leading to self-duality under a generalized Kramers-Wannier duality; analysis of zero-rate code families where logical sector mixing gives subextensive corrections; reformulation of concatenated code decoding as renormalization group flow on a hierarchical lattice.
AI.result: All zero-rate em-symmetric CSS codes share the same optimal code capacity threshold at leading order in a replica limit; self-duality fixes the clean critical point and constrains the disordered phase boundary; self-duality is preserved under code concatenation.
AI.conclusion: There exists a universal framework linking topological, concatenated, and general quantum LDPC code families through self-duality, unifying both optimal thresholds and sub-threshold logical error suppression behavior.

title: Characterising extremal decoherence by quantum measurement incompatibility
summary: Decoherence, when viewed in the Heisenberg picture, can turn incompatible measurements into jointly measurable ones. This provides an observable-level description of emergent classicality in terms of the incompatibility destroyed by a noise channel. The corresponding loss of incompatibility can be captured by the channel's \emph{compatibility region}---the observables in a probe class that become jointly measurable with every noisy observable. The geometry and volume of this region provide a refined operational way to compare noise channels. We apply this framework to decoherence channels, each of which acts by Schur multiplication with extreme points of the convex set of unit-diagonal positive semidefinite matrices. Restricting to extremals eliminates convex mixing and reveals subtle phase-dependent decoherence effects thar are not captured by damping rates or conventional coherence quantifiers. Such channels have a rigid dilation structure described by a rank-one operator frame, which reduces joint measurability to a positivity test, making the compatibility region analytically tractable, and its volume computable from the frame's Gram matrix. If the frame can be normalised to a minimal informationally complete (MIC) POVM, the compatibility region acquires a geometric interpretation in the associated probability representation of the quantum state space, familiar with Qbism. Among maximal-rank extremals, those associated with symmetric informationally complete (SIC) POVMs maximise the compatibility volume and hence destroy the greatest amount of incompatibility, providing an operational characterisation of the special role of SICs in terms of joint measurability. This leads to a new formulation of the well-known SIC existence problem as a joint measurability question for noisy mutually unbiased bases.

AI.tldr: The paper studies decoherence in the Heisenberg picture, showing how noise channels can turn incompatible quantum measurements into jointly measurable ones. The compatibility region—the set of observables that remain jointly measurable after noise—is introduced as a refined tool to compare decoherence channels. Focusing on extremal decoherence channels (Schur multiplication with extreme-point matrices), the authors link joint measurability to positivity via a rank-one operator frame, making the compatibility region analytically tractable. When normalizable to a MIC-POVM, the region gains a Qbist probability-representation interpretation. Among maximal-rank extremals, SIC-POVMs maximize compatibility volume, thus destroying the most incompatibility, which reframes the SIC existence problem as a joint measurability question about noisy mutually unbiased bases.
AI.motivation: To provide an operational, observable-level description of emergent classicality via the destruction of measurement incompatibility by noise channels, and to develop a refined way to compare decoherence channels beyond damping rates or standard coherence quantifiers.
AI.method: The paper analyzes decoherence channels that act by Schur multiplication with extreme points of the convex set of unit-diagonal positive semidefinite matrices. It exploits a rigid dilation structure described by a rank-one operator frame, which reduces joint measurability to a positivity test, making the compatibility region analytically tractable and its volume computable from the frame's Gram matrix. The framework is specialized to extremal channels to eliminate convex mixing and reveal subtle phase-dependent decoherence effects.
AI.result: Among maximal-rank extremals, SIC-POVMs are shown to maximize the compatibility volume, i.e., destroy the greatest amount of incompatibility. This provides an operational characterization of SICs in terms of joint measurability. The SIC existence problem is reformulated as a joint measurability question for noisy mutually unbiased bases.
AI.conclusion: The compatibility region and its volume serve as powerful operational tools for comparing decoherence channels. SICs play a distinguished role in maximizing incompatibility destruction, linking the SIC existence problem to joint measurability in a new way.

title: Basis-independent coherence and quantum correlations in two dipole-dipole-coupled electrons in double quantum-dot molecules
summary: This work examines the thermal dynamics of basis-independent quantum coherence and correlation-based quantum resources for two dipole-dipole-coupled electrons confined in spatially separated quantum-dot (QD) molecules. Single-dot quantum superpositions and inter-subsystem coherence are characterized by using localized and collective coherence. Quantum correlations between the two double quantum dots are quantified by employing Bures distance entanglement, Local quantum uncertainty (LQU), and local quantum Fisher Information (LQFI). The findings show that dipole-dipole coupling $K$ is the most effective protective parameter, extending the entanglement sudden death temperature, diminishing the local quantum superpositions and enhancing the collective coherence. The dipole-dipole interaction has also a crucial impact on protecting LQU and LQFI beyond the entanglement sudden death temperature. Coulomb repulsion $J$ reinforces this protection through an independent channel, projecting the thermal state onto the entangled $\{|0_A 1_B\rangle,|1_A 0_B\rangle\}$ subspace; their combined action is required to approach the entanglement maximum, and it enhances collective coherence and extends the temperature range over which LQU and LQFI remain appreciable. Energy detuning $\varepsilon$ can enhance localized coherence but paradoxically accelerates the entanglement sudden death and quenches LQU and LQFI by weakening two-body correlations. Inter-dot tunneling $Γ$ enhances local superpositions at low temperature, but it reduces collective coherence, lowers the entanglement sudden death temperature, and disrupts other nonclassical correlations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermal quantum resources (coherence and correlations) in two dipole-dipole-coupled electrons in quantum-dot molecules, finding that dipole-dipole coupling K best protects entanglement and correlations, while detuning ε and tunneling Γ have detrimental effects on nonclassical correlations.
AI.motivation: To understand how various physical parameters (dipole-dipole coupling, Coulomb repulsion, energy detuning, inter-dot tunneling) affect the thermal dynamics of quantum coherence and correlation-based resources in spatially separated quantum-dot molecules, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
AI.method: Characterized quantum coherence using localized and collective coherence measures; quantified quantum correlations via Bures distance entanglement, Local quantum uncertainty (LQU), and local quantum Fisher Information (LQFI); systematically varied system parameters (dipole-dipole coupling K, Coulomb repulsion J, energy detuning ε, inter-dot tunneling Γ) to analyze their effects.
AI.result: Dipole-dipole coupling K is the most effective protective parameter, extending entanglement sudden death temperature and enhancing collective coherence. Coulomb repulsion J reinforces protection by projecting onto entangled subspace. Energy detuning ε enhances localized coherence but accelerates entanglement sudden death. Inter-dot tunneling Γ enhances local superpositions at low T but reduces collective coherence and lowers entanglement sudden death temperature.
AI.conclusion: Dipole-dipole coupling combined with Coulomb repulsion is essential for preserving quantum resources at finite temperatures; careful parameter tuning is required to balance competing effects of different physical mechanisms in quantum-dot systems.

title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
summary: Numerous studies have analyzed the use of hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks as a promising alternative to classical deep learning. However, network components on quantum hardware impose fundamental limitations, while the scalability of quantum circuits leads to trainability issues. In this work, we investigate whether small, classically-emulated quantum circuit components can play a meaningful role within complex models, offering an alternative to purely classical convolutional architectures. To this end, we present a systematic study of the effectiveness of a Hybrid Quantum-inspired Convolutional Neural Network (HQiCNN) compared with a parameter-matched classical Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that differs only in an intermediate dense neural layer. Both models are evaluated on two real-world medical datasets while systematically varying the different hyperparameters, ensuring a fair model comparison that is both dataset and hyperparameter independent. The results show that no architecture consistently dominates the other: the HQiCNN achieves its largest gains in intermediate-data regimes, whereas the CNN reaches the highest accuracies for the largest training sets in both datasets. Furthermore, removing entanglement produces comparable performance while enabling substantially better scalability of quantum simulations, and richer observable sets become beneficial only when sufficient training data are available. Finally, we propose two SHAP-based explainability tools for comparing the predictions between both models, $|SHAP|$IoU and $EMD_{pos}$ metric, to demonstrate that both architectures consistently attend to anatomically plausible regions. Thus, we provide a comprehensive benchmark showing that, under certain conditions, hybrid quantum-inspired models are an alternative that can offer benefits in practical tasks such as medical image classification.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically benchmarks a Hybrid Quantum-inspired Convolutional Neural Network (HQiCNN) against a parameter-matched classical CNN on two medical datasets, finding no consistent winner: HQiCNN excels in intermediate-data regimes while classical CNN dominates with larger training sets. The study also examines entanglement removal, observable richness, and introduces SHAP-based explainability metrics to compare model predictions.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether small, classically-emulated quantum circuit components can play a meaningful role within complex models, offering an alternative to purely classical convolutional architectures, given the limitations of quantum hardware and trainability issues in large quantum circuits.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of HQiCNN (with a quantum-inspired intermediate dense layer) versus a parameter-matched classical CNN on two real-world medical datasets, varying hyperparameters across data regimes. SHAP-based explainability tools ($|SHAP|$IoU and $EMD_{pos}$) are proposed to compare model attention regions.
AI.result: No architecture consistently dominates: HQiCNN performs best in intermediate-data regimes, while classical CNN achieves highest accuracy on largest training sets. Removing entanglement yields comparable performance with better scalability. Richer observables benefit only with sufficient data.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid quantum-inspired models can be a viable alternative in practical tasks like medical image classification under certain conditions (e.g., intermediate data availability), but are not universally superior to classical counterparts.

title: Quantum Circuit Fragments and Link Products in Continuous Variables
summary: Quantum circuits are often drawn as complete processes, with fixed inputs and outputs. In many quantum-information tasks, however, the natural object is only a fragment of such a circuit: an unknown source of non-Markovian noise to be probed, a subroutine to be inserted into a larger algorithm, or an agent implementing an adaptive strategy. In finite dimensions, the link product provides a systematic means to analyze how such circuit fragments interact and compose. Here, we develop the corresponding framework for continuous-variable systems. We introduce continuous-variable circuit fragments and associated link products that stitch such fragments together into larger processes. We show that the formalism simplifies substantially in the Gaussian regime, where link products can be evaluated efficiently using covariance-matrix representations. We use the formalism to construct non-Markovian processes and adaptive agent-environment interactions from modular components. This extends the quantum-comb toolkit to continuous variables, providing systematic methods for adaptive sensing, non-Markovian noise mitigation, and higher-order quantum circuit design.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the link product formalism (used for analyzing quantum circuit fragments in finite dimensions) to continuous-variable systems, showing it simplifies in the Gaussian regime via covariance matrices, and enabling construction of non-Markovian processes and adaptive agent-environment interactions.
AI.motivation: Quantum circuits are often treated as complete processes with fixed inputs/outputs, but many tasks involve circuit fragments (e.g., unknown noise sources, subroutines, adaptive agents). No framework existed for systematically composing such fragments in continuous-variable systems.
AI.method: The authors introduce continuous-variable circuit fragments and associated link products for composing them. They show the formalism simplifies in the Gaussian regime, where link products can be evaluated efficiently using covariance-matrix representations.
AI.result: The formalism enables construction of non-Markovian processes and adaptive agent-environment interactions from modular components, extending the quantum-comb toolkit to continuous variables.
AI.conclusion: This work provides systematic methods for adaptive sensing, non-Markovian noise mitigation, and higher-order quantum circuit design in continuous-variable systems.

title: Why Some Quantum States Cannot Be Recovered
summary: The recovery of quantum information after subsystem loss is a central challenge in quantum information processing. However, some states remain beyond the reach of any recovery strategies. Here we identify the algebraic origin of irrecoverability, the ghost information---correlations encoded in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. We introduce a scalar measure quantifying its magnitude and prove a universal error floor below which no virtual recovery map can operate, irrespective of resource investment. We further uncover a spectral phase transition in the sampling cost: bounded when the underlying linear map exhibits a spectrum gap, and divergent with a universal exponent in the gapless regime. Together with the universal error floor, this dichotomy organizes all multipartite quantum states into four classes. Moreover, it is revealed that conditional mutual information---the standard entropic diagnostic---is fundamentally irrelevant to virtual recoverability. As an implication, we show that the error floor imposes a detection threshold for loss-tolerant quantum metrology.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the algebraic origin of irrecoverability in quantum information after subsystem loss—"ghost information" that leaves no trace on accessible subsystems. It introduces a scalar measure, proves a universal error floor for virtual recovery maps, and uncovers a spectral phase transition in sampling cost. These findings organize multipartite quantum states into four classes and reveal that conditional mutual information is irrelevant for virtual recoverability, with implications for loss-tolerant quantum metrology.
AI.motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of recovering quantum information after subsystem loss, specifically why some quantum states cannot be recovered by any strategy, and to identify the algebraic origin of irrecoverability beyond standard entropic diagnostics.
AI.method: The authors identify "ghost information" as the algebraic origin of irrecoverability—correlations encoded in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. They introduce a scalar measure to quantify ghost information, prove a universal error floor for virtual recovery maps, and analyze the spectral properties of the underlying linear map to uncover a phase transition in sampling cost.
AI.result: A universal error floor exists below which no virtual recovery map can operate, regardless of resource investment. A spectral phase transition in sampling cost is uncovered: bounded when the underlying linear map has a spectrum gap, and divergent with a universal exponent in the gapless regime. This dichotomy organizes all multipartite quantum states into four classes. Conditional mutual information is shown to be fundamentally irrelevant to virtual recoverability.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a complete algebraic characterization of quantum recoverability after subsystem loss, establishes fundamental performance bounds, and reveals that the error floor imposes a detection threshold for loss-tolerant quantum metrology, with practical implications for quantum information processing.

title: Tailoring optical Schrödinger cat states via orientation-dependent high-harmonic generation in $\rm{H}_2^+$
summary: We theoretically demonstrate that the molecular orientation angle $θ$ provides a structurally intrinsic, continuously tunable control parameter for engineering optical Schrödinger cat states via high-harmonic generation (HHG) in H$_2^+$. Coupling time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations to the fully quantized HHG framework, we evaluate the Wigner functions of the post-selected harmonic-mode states under two complementary conditioning strategies. Conditioning on resonance-enhanced low-order harmonics exploits the complementary dipole selection rules of the $1σ_g\to1σ_u$ and $1σ_g\to1π_u$ transitions, driving a kitten-cat crossover whose direction is opposite in the two channels as $θ$ is varied. Conditioning on plateau harmonics instead exploits two-center destructive interference, producing a reentrant cat$\to$kitten$\to$cat transition controlled by the order-dependent interference angle $θ^*(q)$. In both cases the crossover is decoupled from the laser intensity, focal geometry, and molecular density, offering a degree of control with no counterpart in atomic targets.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the molecular orientation angle θ in H₂⁺ serves as a structurally intrinsic, continuously tunable control parameter for engineering optical Schrödinger cat states via high-harmonic generation, using two conditioning strategies—resonance-enhanced low-order harmonics and plateau harmonics—to achieve kitten-cat crossovers decoupled from laser parameters and molecular density.
AI.motivation: To establish molecular orientation as a structurally intrinsic, continuously tunable control parameter for optical Schrödinger cat state engineering, offering a degree of control unavailable in atomic targets.
AI.method: The authors couple time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations to a fully quantized HHG framework, evaluating Wigner functions of post-selected harmonic-mode states under two conditioning strategies: (1) resonance-enhanced low-order harmonics exploiting dipole selection rules of 1σ_g→1σ_u and 1σ_g→1π_u transitions, and (2) plateau harmonics exploiting two-center destructive interference controlled by order-dependent interference angle θ^*(q).
AI.result: Conditioning on low-order harmonics drives a kitten-cat crossover with direction opposite in the two channels as θ varies. Conditioning on plateau harmonics produces a reentrant cat→kitten→cat transition. Both crossovers are decoupled from laser intensity, focal geometry, and molecular density.
AI.conclusion: The molecular orientation angle θ provides a unique, continuously tunable control knob for Schrödinger cat state engineering in HHG, with no counterpart in atomic systems.

title: Space-division multiplexed quantum key distribution exploiting multi-plane light conversion for few-mode fibers
summary: As quantum key distribution (QKD) progresses from laboratory demonstrations toward practical deployment, quantum communi- cation networks increasingly require higher key rates and the ability to distribute independent secret keys among multiple users and network nodes. In this paper we present a promsing approach with multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) for demultiplexing entangled photons, transmitted through a few-mode fiber (FMF). We experimentally demonstrated a spatially multiplexed BBM92 QKD scheme. The modes are selectively excited through separate single-mode-fibers and subsequently separated by MPLC into distinct output ports. Unlike high-dimensional QKD based on coherent modal superpositions, our approach exploits distinguishable guided modes as parallel channels while preserving the entanglement required for QKD. For the multiplexed links, we obtain quantum bit error rates of $1.9 \pm 0.4\%$ for the channel 1 and $6.8 \pm 0.8\%$ for the channel 2. These results are relevant for scalable quantum-secured networks, space-division-multiplexed QKD systems, multi-user entanglement distribution, and future quantum internet architectures, where parallel quantum channels must be implemented without compromising the quantum correlations required for security.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a spatially multiplexed BBM92 QKD scheme using multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) to demultiplex entangled photons transmitted through a few-mode fiber (FMF), achieving quantum bit error rates of 1.9% and 6.8% for two parallel channels.
AI.motivation: As QKD moves toward practical deployment, quantum networks require higher key rates and the ability to distribute independent secret keys among multiple users and network nodes, motivating the need for parallel quantum channels.
AI.method: The authors use multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) to demultiplex entangled photons transmitted through a few-mode fiber (FMF). Modes are selectively excited via separate single-mode fibers and separated by MPLC into distinct output ports, implementing a spatially multiplexed BBM92 QKD scheme using distinguishable guided modes as parallel channels.
AI.result: Quantum bit error rates of 1.9 ± 0.4% for channel 1 and 6.8 ± 0.8% for channel 2 were obtained for the multiplexed links.
AI.conclusion: The results are relevant for scalable quantum-secured networks, space-division-multiplexed QKD systems, multi-user entanglement distribution, and future quantum internet architectures requiring parallel quantum channels without compromising quantum correlations.

title: Mixed-Binary Quadratic Programming via QUBO Sampling without Continuous-Variable Binarization
summary: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a finite-temperature formulation for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) that avoids this discretization. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic $p$-median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target experiment, it also reaches the target faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver toward the upper end of the tested range.

AI.tldr: We propose a finite-temperature formulation for separable mixed-binary quadratic programs that avoids discretizing continuous variables by analytically integrating them out, leaving a QUBO over binary variables only. Tested on the quadratic p-median problem, it generates feasible solutions more reliably than penalty-based QUBO and achieves competitive or better accuracy and speed compared to local search and commercial solvers.
AI.motivation: Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing binary dimension and making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. There is a need for methods that handle mixed-binary quadratic programs without this discretization overhead.
AI.method: Develops a finite-temperature formulation for separable mixed-binary quadratic programs where continuous variables are integrated out analytically at fixed Lagrange multipliers, reducing the problem to a QUBO over the original binary variables.
AI.result: On the quadratic p-median problem, the method generates feasible solutions more reliably than penalty-based QUBO; conditional relative error is comparable to local search for small instances and often lower for larger instances; time-to-target is faster than a commercial mixed-integer solver at the upper end of the tested range.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method avoids discretization of continuous variables, improves feasibility over penalty-based approaches, and achieves competitive performance in accuracy and speed for separable MBQPs.

title: Device-Independent Self-Testing of the Three-Qubit CCZ Hypergraph State
summary: The three-qubit CCZ state is the smallest rank-three hypergraph state and an elementary entangled magic resource. Its cubic phase is governed by generalized stabilizers that are not Pauli strings, so standard graph-state self-testing arguments do not apply directly. We show that twenty correlators, all obtainable from five of the eight global input triples in the tripartite two-input, two-output scenario, determine this state and the action of the Pauli $X/Z$ measurements up to local isometries. The proof fixes eight equally weighted computational branches and propagates conditional $X$-flip relations across the branch cube, recovering the minus sign of the $111$ amplitude. These five-context correlations are nonlocal, but the canonical Pauli measurements cannot attain the largest quantum value of any Bell inequality that they violate: whenever they maximize a Bell expression, its local bound has the same value. Introducing an independent third measurement makes self-testing from maximal Bell violation possible. We construct an explicit Bell inequality whose maximal quantum violation self-tests the CCZ state and all three local measurements. An exact sum-of-squares decomposition proves the quantum bound, and its equality conditions yield an analytic SWAP extraction. Together, these results give two explicit device-independent self-tests of the CCZ state and demonstrate that determining a state and its measurements from several correlator equalities is distinct from identifying them through the maximal violation of a single Bell inequality.

AI.tldr: This paper presents two device-independent self-tests of the three-qubit CCZ state: one using five context correlations (twenty correlators from five input triples) that determine the state and Pauli X/Z measurements up to local isometries, and another via a Bell inequality whose maximal quantum violation self-tests the CCZ state and all three local measurements, with an exact sum-of-squares decomposition proving the quantum bound and enabling analytic SWAP extraction.
AI.motivation: The CCZ state is a rank-three hypergraph state and an elementary entangled magic resource, but its cubic phase is governed by generalized stabilizers that are not Pauli strings, so standard graph-state self-testing arguments do not apply directly. The work aims to provide device-independent self-tests for this state despite these challenges.
AI.method: The first self-test fixes eight equally weighted computational branches and propagates conditional X-flip relations across the branch cube, recovering the minus sign of the 111 amplitude using twenty correlators from five global input triples in the tripartite two-input, two-output scenario. The second self-test introduces an independent third measurement and constructs an explicit Bell inequality with an exact sum-of-squares decomposition; equality conditions of the quantum bound yield an analytic SWAP extraction.
AI.result: Twenty correlators from five input triples determine the CCZ state and Pauli X/Z measurements up to local isometries. The canonical Pauli measurements cannot attain the largest quantum value of any Bell inequality they violate (when maximized, local bound equals quantum value). A constructed Bell inequality with maximal quantum violation self-tests the CCZ state and all three local measurements.
AI.conclusion: Two explicit device-independent self-tests of the CCZ state are given. Determining a state and its measurements from several correlator equalities is distinct from identifying them through the maximal violation of a single Bell inequality.

title: Classifying Topology via Edge-State Pure Thermalization
summary: Repeated-interaction machines distinguish heat-like from work-like resources through the steady states they generate, but whether topology can control this distinction remains unknown. Here we reveal the role of topology in the process by showing that topological edge states can act as pure-thermalization fuels. For an open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain used as the fuel source of a micromaser, edge eigenstates suppress both displacement and squeezing and drive the cavity to a Gibbs state, whereas bulk eigenstates activate coherent channels and yield thermo-mechanical operation. This edge-bulk thermodynamic dichotomy remains robust under realistic decoherence, cavity loss, bond disorder, and moderate onsite disorder. We further design a superconducting implementation in which a sixteen-site SSH eigenstate is deterministically compressed into a four-qubit fuel register. The resulting cavity response provides a transport-free classifier of topology and identifies a topology-thermodynamics link that extends beyond cavity-QED to repeated-interaction settings more generally.

AI.tldr: Topological edge states in SSH chains act as pure-thermalization fuels in repeated-interaction machines, suppressing coherent cavity effects and driving Gibbs states, while bulk eigenstates enable thermo-mechanical operation—establishing a topology-thermodynamics link robust to realistic noise.
AI.motivation: To reveal whether topology can control the distinction between heat-like and work-like resources in repeated-interaction machines, specifically by investigating how topological edge states versus bulk eigenstates influence the steady states of a micromaser cavity.
AI.method: Using an open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain as the fuel source for a micromaser; analyzing cavity response to edge vs. bulk eigenstates; testing robustness under decoherence, cavity loss, bond disorder, and onsite disorder; designing a superconducting implementation with deterministic compression of a 16-site SSH eigenstate into a 4-qubit fuel register.
AI.result: Topological edge states suppress displacement and squeezing, driving the cavity to a Gibbs state (pure thermalization); bulk eigenstates activate coherent channels yielding thermo-mechanical operation; this edge-bulk dichotomy remains robust under realistic noise conditions.
AI.conclusion: Topological edge states can serve as pure-thermalization fuels, establishing a topology-thermodynamics link that extends beyond cavity-QED to general repeated-interaction settings, and providing a transport-free classifier of topology via cavity response.

title: Quasiparticle-induced transitions in a fluxonium qubit
summary: Quasiparticles are a prominent decoherence source in superconducting qubits, but their effects are notoriously difficult to isolate in fluxonium. Unlike a transmon, fluxonium is insensitive to offset charge, precluding charge-parity detection of quasiparticle tunneling. We address this challenge by measuring the excitation and de-excitation rates in a fluxonium qubit under controlled on-chip quasiparticle injection. We show that to accurately model the external magnetic flux dependence of the quasiparticle-induced transition rates, it is necessary to account for the superconducting gap asymmetry across the Josephson junctions. A comparison between theory and experiment constrains the relative quasiparticle contributions of the junction array and the small junction and helps explain previously reported discrepancies between the bounds on the quasiparticle densities inferred for these two circuit elements.

AI.tldr: Fluxonium qubit excitation/de-excitation rates under quasiparticle injection reveal that superconducting gap asymmetry across Josephson junctions must be accounted for. This constrains relative quasiparticle contributions from the junction array vs. the small junction, resolving previous density discrepancies.
AI.motivation: Quasiparticles cause decoherence in superconducting qubits, but isolating their effects in fluxonium is challenging because fluxonium is insensitive to offset charge (unlike a transmon), which prevents standard charge-parity detection of quasiparticle tunneling.
AI.method: The authors measure excitation and de-excitation rates in a fluxonium qubit under controlled on-chip quasiparticle injection. They model the external magnetic flux dependence of quasiparticle-induced transition rates, incorporating superconducting gap asymmetry across the Josephson junctions.
AI.result: The superconducting gap asymmetry across the Josephson junctions is necessary to accurately model the flux dependence of quasiparticle-induced transition rates. The model constrains the relative quasiparticle contributions from the junction array and the small junction.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for gap asymmetry resolves previously reported discrepancies between bounds on quasiparticle densities inferred for the two types of circuit elements.

title: Efficient classical simulation of large-scale unitary cluster Jastrow circuits
summary: Recent experiments on quantum computers have challenged the limits of classical computation in chemistry, simulating ground states of strongly correlated molecules. Many of these experiments have utilized the unitary cluster Jastrow ansatz, a quantum circuit inspired by the unitary coupled cluster ansatz that can be tailored to current quantum hardware. Notably, the largest experiment in Sci. Adv. 11, 25 (2025) executed a quantum circuit with 77 qubits and 10,570 gates on an IBM quantum computer and performed classical post-processing with up to 6400 nodes on Fugaku to compute ground state energies better than Hartree-Fock. In this work, we present a polynomial time classical algorithm to compute the energy of any single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuit, independent of locality constraints for quantum hardware. Our algorithm can reproduce the largest experiment from Sci. Adv. 11, 25 (2025) in less than a minute on a laptop, and through circuit optimization enabled by fast simulation we achieve a lower ground state energy than the experiment.

AI.tldr: A polynomial-time classical algorithm computes energies of single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, reproducing a 77-qubit quantum experiment in under a minute on a laptop and achieving lower ground state energy.
AI.motivation: Recent quantum experiments have demonstrated large-scale simulations of strongly correlated molecules using unitary cluster Jastrow circuits on quantum hardware (up to 77 qubits, 10,570 gates), challenging classical limits. The goal is to determine whether such circuits can be simulated classically efficiently, and whether the quantum advantage claim holds.
AI.method: The authors develop a polynomial-time classical algorithm specifically designed for single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, removing hardware-imposed locality constraints. The algorithm is applied to reproduce and optimize the largest experiment from Sci. Adv. 11, 25 (2025).
AI.result: The algorithm reproduces the 77-qubit, 10,570-gate experiment in less than a minute on a laptop. Through circuit optimization enabled by fast simulation, it achieves a lower ground state energy than the original quantum experiment.
AI.conclusion: The claimed boundary of classical computation challenged by this particular quantum experiment is refuted—the circuit class is classically simulable in polynomial time, and classical post-processing can even outperform the quantum result.

title: Floquet Reservoir Engineering for Remote Logical Entanglement
summary: Implementing controlled dissipative dynamics is a powerful approach for state preparation in a variety of contexts, including the preparation of remote entangled states. Here, we show that by going beyond the standard setting of time-independent dissipative dynamics, one can realize even more powerful non-unitary protocols. We introduce dissipative Floquet protocols for stabilizing remote entanglement of logical qubits, where continuously-running dissipation is interleaved with a periodic sequence of unitary gates. These protocols harness existing experimental capabilities, and overcome time-entanglement limits that constrain standard approaches. They also implement an autonomous form of entanglement distillation. We show how these protocols give enhanced protection against waveguide loss, and as an example, analyze a specific implementation using cat-qubits and transmons in a superconducting circuit.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces dissipative Floquet protocols that interleave continuous dissipation with periodic unitary gates to stabilize remote entanglement of logical qubits, overcoming time-entanglement limits and providing autonomous entanglement distillation with enhanced protection against waveguide loss.
AI.motivation: Standard time-independent dissipative dynamics for state preparation are limited by time-entanglement constraints. The authors aim to realize more powerful non-unitary protocols by moving beyond this conventional setting.
AI.method: The authors propose dissipative Floquet protocols that interleave continuously-running dissipation with a periodic sequence of unitary gates to stabilize remote entanglement of logical qubits.
AI.result: The protocols overcome time-entanglement limits that constrain standard approaches, implement autonomous entanglement distillation, and provide enhanced protection against waveguide loss. A specific implementation using cat-qubits and transmons in a superconducting circuit is analyzed.
AI.conclusion: Dissipative Floquet protocols offer a more powerful approach for remote entanglement stabilization, leveraging existing experimental capabilities while providing benefits over standard time-independent dissipative dynamics.

title: A solution to 2-copy distillability of Werner states
summary: Entanglement distillation is a fundamental task in quantum information theory. In this work, we prove that Werner states in arbitrary dimension are 2-copy distillable if and only if they are 1-copy distillable. This answers the longstanding open question of the 2-copy distillability of Werner states. This is an important step on determining whether every non-positive partial transpose (NPT) state is distillable, which remains one of the central open problems in the field of entanglement distillation.

AI.tldr: Proves that Werner states in any dimension are 2-copy distillable iff they are 1-copy distillable, resolving a long-standing open question and advancing toward determining whether all NPT states are distillable.
AI.motivation: To resolve the longstanding open question of whether Werner states are 2-copy distillable, which is a crucial step toward answering the central open problem in entanglement distillation: whether every non-positive partial transpose (NPT) state is distillable.
AI.method: The authors provide a mathematical proof establishing the equivalence between 1-copy and 2-copy distillability for Werner states in arbitrary dimension.
AI.result: Werner states in arbitrary dimension are 2-copy distillable if and only if they are 1-copy distillable.
AI.conclusion: This resolves the open question of 2-copy distillability of Werner states and represents significant progress on the NPT distillability problem, a central open question in entanglement distillation.

title: Cautious optimism for deep parameterized quantum circuits
summary: A central challenge in quantum machine learning is understanding the scaling behavior of parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs). In particular, it remains unclear how their performance on unseen data changes as the number of trainable parameters increases. Prior works have derived formal generalization guarantees for quantum models, but it is well-known that many such results do not fully characterize generalization behavior in practice. In this work, we show that gradient-based PQCs can exhibit improved performance on unseen data as model size increases, displaying the phenomenon of double descent. This contrasts with the traditional view that larger models lead to degraded generalization. We provide analytical results rigorously underpinning this behavior by leveraging add-one-in perturbation techniques and spectral properties of random matrices. We support these results with numerical experiments on re-uploading PQCs across several data sets and training set sizes, consistently observing the predicted double descent behavior. While other obstacles on the path toward practical quantum machine learning remain, our finding that deeper parameterized quantum circuits do not necessarily exhibit degraded performance provides reasons for cautious optimism.

AI.tldr: Gradient-based parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) can exhibit double descent—improved generalization on unseen data as model size increases—challenging the traditional view that larger quantum models lead to worse generalization. This is proven analytically using add-one-in perturbation and random matrix theory, and validated empirically with re-uploading PQCs across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: To resolve the unclear scaling behavior of PQCs in quantum machine learning, specifically whether increasing the number of trainable parameters degrades or improves generalization performance on unseen data.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using add-one-in perturbation techniques and spectral properties of random matrices, combined with numerical experiments on re-uploading PQCs across multiple datasets and training set sizes.
AI.result: Gradient-based PQCs display double descent: performance on unseen data improves as model size increases, contradicting the conventional wisdom that larger quantum models generalize worse. The predicted behavior is consistently observed in numerical experiments.
AI.conclusion: Deeper parameterized quantum circuits do not necessarily exhibit degraded generalization performance, providing cautious optimism for scaling quantum machine learning models despite other remaining obstacles.

title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing
summary: Quantum transfer learning (QTL) is often evaluated by replacing a classical classifier with a fixed variational quantum head, but this hides a key question: when is the quantum branch actually useful? We propose QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing, a selective QTL framework that keeps high-confidence classical predictions and routes only low-confidence samples to a fallback branch. Using a frozen ResNet18 backbone on Fashion-MNIST, we compare manually designed QTL heads, KetGPT-designed quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines under a common data split and optimization schedule. Standard QTL heads reach at most 57.0% accuracy, while the strongest KetGPT head in the main filtered sweep reaches 78.5% accuracy and 0.785 F1-score. Although the strongest fixed classical head remains higher at 81.6%, selective routing gives the quantum branch a clearer role. On low-confidence samples, KetGPT #180 improves accuracy over a parameter-matched MLP fallback by 6.82, 4.31, and 3.03 percentage points at thresholds of 0.70, 0.80, and 0.90. At the full-system level, Adaptive KetGPT-QTL reaches 80.9% accuracy and 0.807 F1-score, outperforming the adaptive classical baseline. A separate compact-circuit ablation identifies KetGPT #160 as a stronger fixed-head candidate, reaching 81.9% accuracy with only 10 quantum parameters and 9 gates. These results suggest that architecture-searched quantum heads are most useful as targeted fallback branches for uncertain inputs rather than uniform replacements for classical classifiers.

AI.tldr: QSTAR selectively routes low-confidence samples to quantum heads, showing that architecture-searched quantum circuits are most useful as targeted fallback branches rather than uniform classical classifier replacements.
AI.motivation: Standard QTL evaluation replaces classical classifiers with fixed variational quantum heads without addressing when quantum components are actually beneficial. The paper aims to identify the precise conditions under which quantum transfer learning provides measurable advantages.
AI.method: Proposes QSTAR (Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing), a selective framework that routes only low-confidence samples to a quantum fallback branch while keeping high-confidence classical predictions. Compares manually designed QTL heads, KetGPT-designed quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines using frozen ResNet18 on Fashion-MNIST.
AI.result: Standard QTL heads: ≤57.0% accuracy. Best KetGPT head: 78.5% accuracy/0.785 F1. Fixed classical head: 81.6% accuracy. On low-confidence samples, KetGPT #180 outperforms parameter-matched MLP by 6.82, 4.31, and 3.03 pp at thresholds 0.70/0.80/0.90. Adaptive KetGPT-QTL: 80.9% accuracy/0.807 F1. KetGPT #160 achieves 81.9% accuracy with only 10 quantum parameters and 9 gates.
AI.conclusion: Architecture-searched quantum heads are most effective as targeted fallback branches for uncertain inputs rather than as uniform replacements for classical classifiers.

title: Exponentially enhanced two-mode multiboson entanglement via phase-modulated tunneling
summary: The entanglement of quantum systems is commonly restricted by their coupling Hamiltonian and initial state properties. Here, we prove by exact analysis of tunnel-coupled bosonic field modes, that factorized multi-boson two-mode states can become fully entangled via stroboscopic sign flips of the two-mode coupling. Their entanglement can exponentially grow with the number of flips. With the exception of specific prohibitive states that are invariant under such sign-flip control, this effect universally applies to two-mode state preparation. Remarkably, this linear control may provide entanglement resources for diverse quantum technological applications by readily available means.

AI.tldr: Factorized multi-boson two-mode states can become fully entangled via stroboscopic sign flips of tunnel coupling, with entanglement growing exponentially with the number of flips, except for specific invariant states.
AI.motivation: To understand how entanglement of quantum systems, typically constrained by the coupling Hamiltonian and initial state, can be enhanced through simple linear control.
AI.method: Exact analysis of tunnel-coupled bosonic field modes with stroboscopic sign flips of the two-mode coupling.
AI.result: Factorized multi-boson two-mode states become fully entangled; entanglement grows exponentially with the number of flips; certain prohibitive invariant states are exempt.
AI.conclusion: Linear sign-flip control universally applies to two-mode state preparation and may provide entanglement resources for quantum technologies via readily available means.

title: QuantumChain: Blockchain-Backed Quantum Federated Learning for Financial Fraud Detection
comment: Accepted at the IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE), 2026
summary: Financial fraud detection is challenged by decentralized data, severe class imbalance, and privacy constraints. This paper presents QuantumChain, a secure Quantum Federated Learning (QFL) framework that combines hybrid quantum-classical neural networks, encrypted federated aggregation, blockchain-based auditability, and quantum-secure communication. Each client trains a local hybrid model in which a variational quantum circuit is embedded between classical neural layers, while model updates are protected through homomorphic encryption, threshold secret sharing, and QKD-based keying. A permissioned blockchain records aggregation events and supports reputation-weighted trust among participants. We evaluate QuantumChain on financial transaction data using a compact, size-matched classical baseline to isolate the effect of the quantum layer. Results show that the HQNN achieves comparable accuracy while improving fraud-class recall in most settings, reaching 94.6% recall compared with 93.2% for the classical model. The Deep QLayer improves performance in full-data settings, suggesting that added circuit depth helps recover representational capacity when the shallow circuit becomes limited. Mixed-state simulations further show that the recall trend persists under non-ideal quantum evolution. In federated deployment with 10 heterogeneous clients, global accuracy increases from 97.7% to 98.8% over five rounds before stabilizing. These results show that QuantumChain can integrate depth-aware hybrid quantum models into a secure federated fraud-detection pipeline while maintaining stable global convergence.

AI.tldr: QuantumChain is a secure quantum federated learning framework for financial fraud detection that integrates hybrid quantum-classical neural networks, homomorphic encryption, blockchain auditability, and QKD-based security. It achieves 94.6% fraud recall (vs. 93.2% classical) and 98.8% global accuracy under federated settings.
AI.motivation: Financial fraud detection faces three key challenges: decentralized data silos across institutions, severe class imbalance (fraud vs. legitimate transactions), and strict privacy regulations. Existing approaches cannot simultaneously address all three constraints.
AI.method: QuantumChain combines (1) hybrid quantum-classical neural networks with variational quantum circuits embedded between classical layers (including a deeper "Deep QLayer" variant), (2) encrypted federated aggregation via homomorphic encryption and threshold secret sharing, (3) QKD-based keying for quantum-secure communication, and (4) permissioned blockchain for auditability and reputation-weighted trust.
AI.result: The HQNN achieves 94.6% fraud recall vs. 93.2% for the classical baseline. Deep QLayer improves performance in full-data settings. In federated deployment with 10 heterogeneous clients, global accuracy rises from 97.7% to 98.8% over five rounds. Mixed-state simulations confirm recall trends persist under non-ideal quantum noise.
AI.conclusion: QuantumChain demonstrates that depth-aware hybrid quantum models can be securely integrated into a federated fraud-detection pipeline, achieving stable global convergence while improving fraud-class recall under privacy-preserving, decentralized conditions.

title: Directional telecom photons from a chirally coupled quantum dot
summary: Chiral quantum light-matter interfaces, where the internal spin state of a quantum emitter determines the direction in which it emits, are essential building blocks of non-reciprocal quantum devices, deterministic quantum logical gates and entanglement generation protocols. Yet, a chiral quantum interface that operates at telecom wavelengths, and is compatible with telecommunication infrastructure and silicon photonics, does not yet exist. Here, we report on an integrated chiral quantum interface in the original telecom band (1260-1360 nm), created by interfacing InAs quantum dots with a waveguide-coupled InP microdisk. We tune the quantum dot transitions through the photonic cavity using a strong magnetic field, observing a peak cavity enhancement of 3.3 and an emission directionality of 0.985, demonstrating the near-ideal chiral quantum coupling required for quantum information processing on integrated photonic devices.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the first chiral quantum light-matter interface operating in the telecom O-band (1260-1360 nm), integrating InAs quantum dots with an InP microdisk waveguide. Using a strong magnetic field to tune quantum dot transitions, they achieve a cavity enhancement of 3.3 and emission directionality of 0.985, enabling near-ideal chiral coupling for integrated quantum photonics.
AI.motivation: Existing chiral quantum interfaces lack operation at telecom wavelengths compatible with existing telecommunication infrastructure and silicon photonics, which is essential for practical quantum networks and integrated photonic devices.
AI.method: InAs quantum dots are interfaced with a waveguide-coupled InP microdisk. A strong magnetic field is applied to tune quantum dot transitions through the photonic cavity, enabling control over chiral light-matter coupling.
AI.result: Peak cavity enhancement of 3.3 and emission directionality of 0.985 were observed, demonstrating near-ideal chiral quantum coupling at telecom O-band wavelengths.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first telecom-band chiral quantum interface, paving the way for non-reciprocal quantum devices, deterministic quantum gates, and entanglement generation on integrated photonic platforms.

title: Rack-integrated quantum dot-based source of single and entangled photons at telecom C-band
summary: For quantum light sources in everyday telecommunication networks, quantum science needs to be fully transformed into quantum technology. The first necessary step to move outside a well-controlled lab environment requires the use of quantum light sources operating in the technologically relevant telecom O- and C-band. This can be provided using epitaxial quantum dots as deterministic sources of quantum light. Particularly intriguing is that emitters operating at telecom wavelengths are rapidly catching up with their short wavelength counterparts in terms of performances. Here, we make a decisive step forward in the development of quantum communication networks: a state-of-the-art source of quantum light, a semiconductor quantum dot (QD), with record coincidence rate for entangled photon emission in the telecom C-band, is operated inside an optimized rack-based setup. This setup includes a tunable pulsed laser for the QD excitation (from quasi- to fully resonant excitation), all optics for the excitation filtering, and QD signal coupling into single-mode fibers. Overall, the setup allows for above $50\%$ transmission for both exciton and biexciton photons. These results show that quantum dots-based telecom light sources can now be transported and integrated into existing fiber infrastructures, an important step to demonstrate the feasibility of the upcoming quantum internet.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a rack-based, transportable telecom C-band quantum dot source with record entangled photon coincidence rates and >50% transmission, marking a key step toward practical quantum internet integration.
AI.motivation: To move quantum light sources from well-controlled lab environments into real-world telecommunication networks, enabling practical quantum communication technologies.
AI.method: A semiconductor quantum dot (QD) emitting entangled photons in the telecom C-band is integrated into an optimized rack-based setup with a tunable pulsed laser (quasi- to fully resonant excitation), excitation filtering optics, and single-mode fiber coupling.
AI.result: Record coincidence rate for entangled photon emission in the telecom C-band; above 50% transmission for both exciton and biexciton photons.
AI.conclusion: Quantum dot-based telecom light sources can now be transported and integrated into existing fiber infrastructures, demonstrating feasibility for the upcoming quantum internet.

title: An Optimal Analysis of the Product Test
summary:
Product testing, i.e., deciding whether a pure multipartite quantum state is fully unentangled across a specified tensor decomposition, serves as a bridge between quantum property testing, unentangled quantum proof systems, and tensor optimization. Despite being a fundamental property testing task and having many applications, the product test's exact (worst-case) acceptance probability curve has yet to be fully determined. In this work, we determine this curve exactly. Let $ω$ be the maximum squared overlap of the input with a product state, and let $\mathrm{PT}_n(ω)$ be the largest possible acceptance probability of the product test over all $n$-partite pure states with product overlap $ω$, allowing arbitrary finite local dimensions. We prove that, for every $n\ge 2 $ and every $ω\in(0,1] $, $$
  \mathrm{PT}_n(ω)=\frac12\left(1+mω^2+(1-mω)^2\right), $$ where $m=\lfloor1/ω\rfloor $. The formula recovers the previously known tight section of the curve for $ω\ge 1/2 $, resolves all low-overlap regimes $ω<1/2 $, and implies $\mathrm{PT}_n(ω)\to 1/2 $ as $ω\to 0$ answering an open problem in [Soleimanifar and Wright, SODA 2022]. As a complexity-theoretic application, our results improve the one-shot soundness parameter in the Harrow-Montanaro reduction from $\mathsf{QMA}(k)$ to $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$. Our techniques, built upon those of Soleimanifar and Wright, allow us to resolve these open questions while remaining surprisingly elementary.

AI.tldr: This paper exactly determines the worst-case acceptance probability curve of the product test for pure multipartite entangled states, resolving open problems from Soleimanifar and Wright (SODA 2022). The formula shows that the maximum acceptance probability depends on the maximum squared overlap ω with a product state via PT_n(ω)=1/2(1+mω²+(1-mω)²) where m=⌊1/ω⌋, with implications for QMA(2) soundness.
AI.motivation: The product test is a fundamental primitive connecting quantum property testing, unentangled quantum proofs, and tensor optimization. Despite its importance, the exact acceptance probability curve was unknown for low-overlap regimes (ω < 1/2), and the limiting behavior as ω→0 was an open problem. Determining this curve is essential for understanding the test's capabilities and for applications in complexity theory.
AI.method: The authors build upon techniques from Soleimanifar and Wright, proving an exact formula for PT_n(ω) that works for all n ≥ 2 and all ω ∈ (0,1]. The proof involves analyzing the maximum acceptance probability over all n-partite pure states with a given product overlap ω, allowing arbitrary finite local dimensions. The approach remains elementary despite resolving several open questions.
AI.result: The exact formula PT_n(ω)=1/2(1+mω²+(1-mω)²) with m=⌊1/ω⌋ recovers the known tight section for ω ≥ 1/2, resolves all low-overlap regimes ω < 1/2, and shows PT_n(ω)→1/2 as ω→0. As an application, the results improve the one-shot soundness parameter in the Harrow-Montanaro reduction from QMA(k) to QMA(2).
AI.conclusion: The paper fully characterizes the product test's worst-case acceptance probability curve, closing open problems in the field. The elementary techniques and exact formula provide a complete understanding of this fundamental test, with direct implications for quantum complexity theory, particularly for QMA proof systems.

title: Flow of local sensitivity in a spin chain coupled to a bosonic bath
summary: We study how local sensitivity to an encoded parameter, captured by the quantum Fisher information, flows between a spin chain, a coupled bosonic bath, and their quantum correlations, where we treat the bath as a full many-body quantum system beyond the Lindbladian approximation. We analyze how the coupling symmetry determines the destination of the departed sensitivity directly at the level of the Hamiltonian. We consider an excitation-exchanging Jaynes--Cummings coupling, which preserves the total number of excitations, and a spin-excitation-conserving Holstein coupling. We find that the Holstein coupling leaves the bath with no first-order information about the phase and stores the lost sensitivity entirely in spin--bath correlations, whereas the Jaynes--Cummings coupling passes this sensitivity to the bath, in full for a single excitation. The bath spectrum then governs whether the sensitivity ever returns to the spins. It revives fully and periodically when the coupled-system frequencies share a common period, but when those frequencies disperse the departed share dephases across the bath modes and never returns. We note that a transported metrological register loses more sensitivity than its arrival fidelity implies.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how quantum Fisher information (sensitivity to a parameter) flows between a spin chain, a bosonic bath, and their quantum correlations beyond the Lindbladian approximation. The Holstein coupling stores lost sensitivity entirely in spin-bath correlations, while Jaynes-Cummings coupling transfers it to the bath, with revival depending on the bath spectrum.
AI.motivation: To understand how local parameter sensitivity (quantum Fisher information) flows in a full many-body quantum system beyond the Markovian/Lindbladian approximation, particularly how coupling symmetry determines where the departed sensitivity ends up.
AI.method: The authors analyze two coupling types at the Hamiltonian level: (1) excitation-exchanging Jaynes-Cummings coupling (preserving total excitation number) and (2) spin-excitation-conserving Holstein coupling. They track quantum Fisher information flow among spin chain, bosonic bath, and their correlations.
AI.result: Holstein coupling leaves the bath with no first-order phase information and stores all lost sensitivity in spin-bath correlations. Jaynes-Cummings coupling passes sensitivity to the bath (fully for a single excitation). Sensitivity revival depends on whether the coupled-system frequencies share a common period (full periodic revival) or are dispersed (dephasing and no return). Transported metrological register loses more sensitivity than its arrival fidelity implies.
AI.conclusion: The coupling symmetry fundamentally determines the destination of lost quantum Fisher information. Sensitivity can be fully recoverable under commensurate frequencies but permanently lost under dispersion, with implications for quantum metrology and information transport.

title: Extended Single-Atom Tweezer Arrays in High-Cooperativity Cavity-QED
summary: A central challenge for cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is to make high-cooperativity optical interfaces compatible with site-resolved arrays of single atoms. Here, we demonstrate optical tweezer arrays of individual $^{87}$Rb atoms inside a fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity with single-atom cooperativity $\mathcal{C} \sim 90$. We combine background-free site-resolved fluorescence imaging of extended arrays with collective coupling to a common cavity mode for arrays with a mean atom number up to $\bar{N} \simeq 36$. These results establish a high-cooperativity platform for many-body cavity-QED with site-resolved detection and control.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates optical tweezer arrays of individual rubidium atoms inside a fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity with single-atom cooperativity ~90, combining site-resolved fluorescence imaging with collective cavity coupling for arrays up to ~36 atoms, establishing a high-cooperativity platform for many-body cavity-QED.
AI.motivation: A central challenge for cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is to make high-cooperativity optical interfaces compatible with site-resolved arrays of single atoms.
AI.method: Optical tweezer arrays of individual ⁸⁷Rb atoms are placed inside a fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity, achieving single-atom cooperativity C ~ 90. Background-free site-resolved fluorescence imaging is used alongside collective coupling to a common cavity mode.
AI.result: Arrays with mean atom number up to N̄ ≃ 36 were demonstrated, with combined site-resolved imaging and collective cavity coupling.
AI.conclusion: These results establish a high-cooperativity platform for many-body cavity-QED with site-resolved detection and control.

title: Unified theory of classical and quantum semiparametric efficiency
summary: In classical and quantum statistics, high-dimensional unknown parameters are abundant and it is often prudent to make minimal assumptions about them using so-called semiparametric models. To attack a wide range of semiparametric problems in one broad stroke, we present a unified treatment of statistical efficiency for classical and quantum semiparametric models, generalizing the Cramér-Rao and Helstrom bounds beyond finite-dimensional parameters. We introduce the fundamental concepts in abstract and geometric terms before applying them to many examples, covering general classical and quantum models as well as the paradigmatic special cases of Gaussian and Poisson fields. We give an in-depth treatment of channels in the semiparametric efficiency theory and advocate the use of the singular value decomposition to elucidate the statistical effects of channels. To demonstrate the utility of the formalism, we apply it to coherent and incoherent optical imaging problems, assuming an arbitrary field or intensity on the object plane without parametric assumptions. Our formalism enables us to compute classical and quantum limits to coherent and incoherent imaging resolution in statistical terms. For subdiffraction incoherent imaging, we demonstrate that spatial-mode demultiplexing can be far superior to direct imaging in estimating generalized Fourier coefficients and come closer to the quantum limits. We envision our theory becoming an essential tool for both classical and quantum statistics with useful applications to sensing and imaging, whenever minimal assumptions about a high-dimensional parameter should be made.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified treatment of statistical efficiency for both classical and quantum semiparametric models, generalizing the Cramér-Rao and Helstrom bounds beyond finite-dimensional parameters. Using geometric and abstract concepts, it covers general models, Gaussian and Poisson fields, and channels via singular value decomposition. Applied to coherent and incoherent optical imaging, it demonstrates that spatial-mode demultiplexing outperforms direct imaging for subdiffraction estimation, approaching quantum limits.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional unknown parameters are common in both classical and quantum statistics, and minimal assumptions via semiparametric models are desirable. The authors aim to provide a unified theoretical framework that bridges classical and quantum semiparametric efficiency, enabling analysis of problems where parameters are infinite-dimensional and assumptions are minimal.
AI.method: The authors develop an abstract geometric formalism for semiparametric efficiency, generalizing the Cramér-Rao bound (classical) and Helstrom bound (quantum) to infinite-dimensional parameter spaces. They advocate singular value decomposition for channels in semiparametric theory. The framework is applied to coherent and incoherent optical imaging with arbitrary field/intensity assumptions.
AI.result: The formalism yields classical and quantum limits to coherent and incoherent imaging resolution. In subdiffraction incoherent imaging, spatial-mode demultiplexing is shown to be far superior to direct imaging for estimating generalized Fourier coefficients, achieving performance closer to quantum limits.
AI.conclusion: The theory is envisioned as an essential tool for both classical and quantum statistics, particularly useful for sensing and imaging applications where high-dimensional parameters must be estimated under minimal assumptions.

title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
summary: Formal verification is becoming increasingly practical for quantum computing, yet the ability of AI agents to construct machine-checkable proofs in this domain remains unmeasured. We introduce Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench and Lean-QIT-Bench, two Lean 4 benchmarks containing 36 and 40 theorem-completion tasks for quantum algorithms and quantum information theory, respectively. Every task compiles in a fixed environment and is evaluated by deterministic proof checking and targeted semantic review, with difficulty weights assigned before model execution. We evaluate four models-GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, and MiniMax M3-within a common theorem-proving framework under two settings: a task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD), which additionally provides access to a verified domain library. The highest difficulty-weighted scores are 60.4 out of 100 on the quantum-algorithm benchmark and 59.6 out of 100 on the quantum-information benchmark. LAD improves both score and completion rate in all eight model-benchmark comparisons, with gains of up to 15.9 points, providing evidence that verified libraries can strengthen domain-specific proof agents. The results reveal recurring weaknesses of agentic proving in areas such as quantum simulation, quantum learning, quantum information measures, and entanglement theory. Monetary and wall-clock costs per score point also vary substantially across models, highlighting important capability-efficiency trade-offs. We expect these benchmarks to establish a reproducible baseline for developing more capable and reliable proof agents, and to pave the way toward self-evolving AI scientists for advancing quantum information science.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces two Lean 4 benchmarks (Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench and Lean-QIT-Bench) for evaluating AI agents' ability to construct machine-checkable proofs in quantum computing. Four models are tested under baseline and library-augmented deduction settings, achieving highest scores of 60.4 and 59.6 out of 100. Library-augmented deduction consistently improves performance. The work establishes reproducible baselines for developing proof agents in quantum information science.
AI.motivation: Formal verification is becoming practical for quantum computing, but the capability of AI agents to construct machine-checkable proofs in this domain has not been systematically measured. The paper aims to fill this gap.
AI.method: Two Lean 4 benchmarks are created (36 tasks for quantum algorithms, 40 for quantum information theory). Four models (GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, MiniMax M3) are evaluated under two settings: task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD). Evaluation uses deterministic proof checking and targeted semantic review with pre-assigned difficulty weights.
AI.result: Highest scores: 60.4/100 (quantum algorithms) and 59.6/100 (quantum information). LAD improves scores and completion rates in all eight model-benchmark comparisons, with gains up to 15.9 points. Recurring weaknesses in quantum simulation, learning, information measures, and entanglement theory. Substantial cost variations across models.
AI.conclusion: The benchmarks establish a reproducible baseline for developing capable proof agents. Verified libraries strengthen domain-specific proof agents. The work paves the way toward self-evolving AI scientists for quantum information science.

title: Beyond Calabrese-Cardy Scaling: Exceptional-Point Sensitivity from the de Sitter RT Surface
summary: Entanglement entropy at one-dimensional criticality typically follows the Calabrese-Cardy scaling. In non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points, however, we show that the biorthogonal entropy of a finite system retains an additional sensitivity to a small energy gap \(Δ\) even when \(Δ< 1/L\). On top of the usual Calabrese-Cardy term, we find an interval-independent contribution \(S_{\rm res}=\log(ΔL)\), visible as a vertical offset and detectable even for a one-site subsystem. This behavior has no Hermitian analogue: a sub-finite-size gap is effectively invisible to entanglement in unitary critical chains, whereas here the entropy continues to resolve such a gap through its dependence on \(ΔL\). We interpret the result within the de Sitter geometry generated by non-unitary continuous multiscale entanglement renormalization: because the dS extremal surface reaches the IR endpoint, entanglement necessarily retains the endpoint contribution. On a finite ring, a regular circuit cannot terminate at a one-site product state and instead leaves an entangled two-site IR state. Computing the entanglement of the IR state recovers the same \(\log(ΔL)\) term, identifying this additional long-range entanglement as the residual entropy left after finite-depth disentangling.

AI.tldr: In non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points, biorthogonal entanglement entropy exhibits an extra log(ΔL) term even when the gap Δ < 1/L, unlike Hermitian chains. This residual entropy, visible as a vertical offset even for a one-site subsystem, arises from de Sitter geometry in cMERA where the IR endpoint contributes, and corresponds to long-range entanglement in a two-site IR state inaccessible to finite-depth disentangling.
